items.title: [Bug] Modular MoE reports zero local experts after a backend releases source weights
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Bug

A modular MoE backend that prepares its own expert-weight owner and then releases the source weights fails during startup profiling because `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl` derives `local_num_experts` from `w1.shape[0]`.

The downstream B12X EP integration reproduces this with GLM-5.2 NVFP4, TP8/DCP4/EP8 on 8x RTX PRO 6000:

```text
ValueError: B12X EP local expert metadata does not match prepared weights: metadata=0, prepared=32
```

Failing run + logs: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/30186408654/job/89751956320

## Cause

B12X intentionally replaces the source `w13`/`w2` parameters with empty tensors after preparing its packed expert owner. The generic modular wrapper subsequently reports zero local experts, while the backend-owned prepared weights still contain the correct 32.

The backend's `moe_problem_size()` can recover the prepared expert count, but the modular path does not use that value for workspace metadata.

## Expected

Released source weights should not erase backend-owned expert metadata, and real expert-count mismatches should continue to fail.

items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On ROCm, the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool sparse indexer **silently overwrites its own KV cache**. 4096 pool entries are written into 864 distinct slots, so ~79 % of the indexer's keys are wrong. The model still produces fluent text, so nothing crashes — long-context recall just degrades, and `temperature=0` stops being reproducible because the damage depends on which physical blocks the allocator hands out.

This is **ROCm-only** and distinct from #40018 (whose fix, #43781, is present in the tree I tested).

### Root cause

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
return [1, MultipleOf(16)] if current_platform.is_rocm() else [64]
```

On CUDA the backend declares exactly `[64]`, so vLLM sets `kernel_block_size = 64`, `BlockTable.use_hybrid_blocks = True`, and builds a kernel-granular block table. On ROCm it declares "any multiple of 16", so the hybrid aligner's choice (640 tokens here) is taken as natively supported: `blocks_per_kv_block == 1`, **no kernel-granular block table**.

But the kernels do not read 640-token blocks. DeepGEMM/AITER paged-MQA reads pool pages of 32 states; with `tokens_per_state == index_kpool == 4` that is 128 tokens. So the storage block (640 tok = 160 states) is five pages, and both `slot_mapping` and `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` address it with the **page** size (32) while the block table holds **spec-block** ids — a 5x over-subscription.

The intended split is even documented in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py` as `storage_kernel_block_size`, but that identifier appears nowhere else in the tree — it was never implemented.

|---|---|---|
| distinct cache slots written (of 4096 pools) | **864** | **4096** |

items.title: [Bug]: KDA/gated-delta-rule chunked-scan buffers are outside memory profiling — runtime OOM at large --max-num-batched-tokens
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

The chunked-scan buffers in the gated-delta-rule (KDA) path scale linearly with
`--max-num-batched-tokens`, are allocated transiently inside the forward pass, and are **not
covered by vLLM's startup memory profiling**. The KV cache is therefore sized as if that memory
were free, and above a certain chunk size the engine dies at runtime — mid-request, after having
served traffic.

### Observed

GLM-5.3-Flash (45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention + 11 sparse MLA), 1× MI350X (gfx950),
ROCm 7.2.3, TP1, MXFP4 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.
16 concurrent requests of ~38k tokens each.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | successful | failed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 192 … 65 536 | 16 / 16 | 0 | stable across 3 runs each |
| **81 920** | **5 / 16** | **11** | engine shut down |
| **131 072** | **4 / 16** | 12 | engine shut down |

```
(Worker) ERROR  File ".../flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk_delta_h.py", line 357,
                  in chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
(Worker) ERROR    v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None
(Worker) ERROR  torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB.
                  GPU 0 has a total capacity of 287.98 GiB of which 0 [bytes is free]
(APIServer) INFO [shutdown] EngineCore process manager: using 15.0s ROCm cleanup grace
                  after immediate request abort
```

Startup reported no problem — `GPU KV cache size: 6,940,947 tokens` at 81,920, and the memory
profiling line looked healthy.

### Mechanism

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` allocates two buffers proportional to the token count in the batch:

```python
B, T, Hg, K, V = *k.shape, u.shape[-1]
H  = u.shape[-2]
BT = chunk_size                      # FLA_CHUNK_SIZE = 64, hard-coded in ops/utils.py:31
...
N, NT = len(cu_seqlens) - 1, len(chunk_indices)
h     = k.new_empty(B, NT, H, V, K)          # NT = ceil(T / 64)  -> linear in T
v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None

items.title: [Bug][DCP] GLM-5.3 dense prefill consumes uninitialized K rows on non-owner ranks
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Problem

Following the GLM-5.3 report in #50095, TP4/DCP4 generation with Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 is deterministically incoherent while matched TP4/DCP1 is coherent. This remains after applying the earlier #50005 correctness fix and after disabling the direct DCP communication paths, so it is a separate bug.
The GLM-5.3 problem is originally reported by @ehfd 

### Root cause

NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 dense prefill requests normalized/rotated K materialization from fused_norm_rope on every DCP rank. The fused kernel currently returns when slot_mapping is negative. Under DCP, a negative local slot can mean that another rank owns the cache row; it does not mean that the dense-prefill K row is unused. As a result, non-owner ranks leave kv_c_out and k_pe_out uninitialized, and dense prefill consumes those buffers.

Cache ownership and K materialization need separate guards: materialize the requested K outputs on every rank, but retain the negative-slot guard before owner-local cache writes.

### Validation

On 4x GB200 with greedy decoding, chunked prefill, prefix caching, FP8 KV cache, and CUDA graphs enabled, the narrow fix makes DCP4 token output exactly match DCP1 for:

- 512 uncached prompt tokens: SHA256 222258a1...
- 1536 uncached prompt tokens: SHA256 76643708...
- 1024 cached plus 1536 uncached prompt tokens: SHA256 4a150ea6...

The model run used the matching cu130 binary/source pair at 570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e with #50005 and the narrow fix overlaid. The same failing guard is unchanged on current main ee3c00bbf47e0ef7e975705cc980b06ee5576bb0; a current-main native build is still in progress and will be added to the PR validation.

A focused current-main regression test also passes and verifies that K outputs are materialized while MLA/indexer caches remain untouched on a non-owner rank.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] Sparse-MLA indexer reserves a 32 GiB decode-logits workspace during profiling (max_num_batched_tokens rows), costing 21 % of the KV cache
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

On ROCm, the sparse-MLA indexer reserves the decode logits workspace at the theoretical upper bound during the memory profiling run, not at the bound the scheduler can actually produce. On a 1M-context model that single allocation is **32 GiB per GPU**, and since `WorkspaceManager.lock()` freezes the size after profiling, it is subtracted from the KV cache for the lifetime of the process.

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, profiling early-exit branch of `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`:

```python
# Decode logits buffer, used by rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits.
# batch_size * next_n <= hidden_states.shape[0] == max_num_batched_tokens
if _ON_GFX942 or _ON_GFX950:
    workspace_manager.get_simultaneous(
        ((hidden_states.shape[0], max_model_len), torch.float32),
    )
```

The comment states the bound correctly, but `max_num_batched_tokens` is a *prefill* bound. A decode step produces at most `max_num_seqs * (num_speculative_tokens + 1)` rows — for us 64 · 4 = 256, against the 8192 that get reserved.

## Evidence

Full GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`), TP4 on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, `max_model_len` 1048576, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, `max_num_seqs` 64, MTP k=3, fp8 KV, block size 16.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool 32-page split (hybrid block_size=1152) GPU Memory access fault on MTP decode
items.bodyExcerpt:
ROCm gfx942, GLM-5.3-Flash, hybrid KDA + MLA + kpool indexer: after the hybrid aligner lands on `cache_config.block_size = 1152`, the kpool indexer virtually splits 288-entry storage into **32-entry** paged-MQA pages. MTP decode then dies with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N` (one `VllmWorker` abort → engine down). Not OOM.

Line numbers below are **vLLM `main` @ `156050598eea0bb1124b9c106b22ba4a8c56f82a`** (2026-09-04). Runtime numbers are from a gfx942 serving image derived from #53906 plus later local patches; they are labelled as such.

## Environment (runtime)

- 8× MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=4, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`
- Hybrid KDA + MLA + kpool indexer (`index_kpool = 4`)
- Serving image: #53906-era tree. Crash B already included the V2 slot-mapping `in_range` guard from #54296.

## Symptom

Two serving aborts on 2026-09-03, same family:

- Crash A (03:41Z): ~41054 computed tokens, first MTP decode after that prefill. Image did **not** yet have the #54296 V2 guard.
- Crash B (09:18Z): 5-way mixed batch (4 MTP decode + one 2304-token chunked prefill). `new_block_ids` around **3809–3813**. Prefix-cache hit ~93%, KV usage ~4.25%. Image **already had** the #54296 V2 guard.

Banner is `Memory access fault by GPU node-N` → that rank’s `VllmWorker` exits → engine down. Not OOM. An aiter GEMM-shape miss in the same logs is not sufficient (same shape had been served earlier without abort). `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens=[-1,-1]` is the async placeholder, not the address.

## Why 1152 becomes a 32-page split

`PAGED_MQA_PAGE_SIZES = (32, 64)` (`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:35`).

`Glm5NextIndexerCache.get_kv_cache_spec` (`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py:145-152`; there is no `amd/attention.py` sibling) picks the virtual page as:

- native if `storage_block_size <= 64`
- 64 if `storage_block_size % 64 == 0`
- **else 32**

On this host the hybrid mamba aligner set `block_size = 1152`. With `index_kpool = 4`:

`1152 / 4 = 288`, `288 > 64`

items.title: [ROCm] Support unlimited sequence lengths via multi-pass reduction
items.bodyExcerpt:
At present, on ROCm for certain models including GLM-4.7, vLLM has a choice between two attention implementations from vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py. One is a very slow reference Triton kernel and the other is a hand-coded op. The custom op only supports context length up to 131072 tokens, which means that, unless vLLM is set to eager mode, it'll only be used if max_seq_len is <131072 (otherwise, since actual context length is unknown at graph capture time, it defaults to Triton for all context lengths). This patch drops the 131072 token cap and adds a multi-pass mode to support unlimited max_seq_len. It also adds unit tests to cover this scenario. This results in a drastic increase in token generation throughput on ROCm for GLM-4.7 for max_seq_len>131072. *quantized* MoE method**, so the allocated parameters do not match the checkpoint
tensors.

The trigger in both cases is the MTP (speculative-decoding drafter) layer. AMD's
Quark and community GPTQ quantizations of `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` quantize the 40
transformer layers but leave the MTP layer's experts in bf16. The main model
loads fine; only the drafter fails.

* **Original MXFP4/Quark report** (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must
  match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1`, in
  `routed_experts.py::_load_w2`).
  `hidden_size=2048`, `moe_intermediate_size=512`. Quark MXFP4 allocates
  `w2_weight` as `(E, hidden, intermediate // 2)` = `(E, 2048, 256)` (fp4 packs
  two values per byte), while the checkpoint's MTP `down_proj.weight` is the
  unquantized `(2048, 512)`. `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`'s
  `quantization_config.exclude` lists `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.<i>.{gate,up,down}_proj`
  for all 256 experts, but `should_ignore_layer()` only compared the *parent*
  layer name `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts` against those *child* entries.
  **This half is already fixed on main** by the `check_children` argument added
  to `quark/utils.py::should_ignore_layer` (the amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 fix), which is
  why a commenter on the issue could not reproduce it on main. No change needed.

* **Still-broken GPTQ report** (issue comments:
  `AttributeError: 'RoutedExperts' object has no attribute 'w2_weight'. Did you
  mean: 'w2_qweight'?`, same drafter-loading path).
  `AutoGPTQConfig` tracks which modules the checkpoint actually quantized in
  `modules_in_block_to_quantize` — auto-derived in `maybe_update_config()` from

## Purpose

Fixes #49649.

AITER has **no non-persistent** sparse-MLA decode kernel for `gqa_ratio == 64` fp8/fp8:

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable RAM-guarded safetensors auto-prefetch when the checkpoint filesystem is reported as `virtiofs`.

The default loading mode currently detects `VIRTIOFS` but leaves prefetch disabled because the automatic allowlist contains only NFS, NFS4, and Lustre. With a 1403.19 GiB GLM-5.2 checkpoint that fit within available RAM, explicit prefetch reduced model loading from 1597.0 seconds to 70.7 seconds, about 22.6x.

This change:

- adds VirtioFS to the existing automatic prefetch set;
- renames the internal network-filesystem classification because VirtioFS is a host/guest shared filesystem, not a network filesystem;
- documents default and explicit-lazy behavior;
- adds behavior coverage for VirtioFS, the RAM guard, explicit `lazy`, and a local filesystem.

### Safety and scope

Automatic prefetch still activates only when `safetensors_load_strategy` is unset and total checkpoint size is at most 90% of available RAM. Explicit `lazy` remains an opt-out.

VirtioFS backing storage, cache policy, and DAX configuration vary. The filesystem type alone does not prove that storage is high latency or that prefetched guest pages will be retained. 

This changes startup I/O scheduling only. Loaded tensor values and model outputs are unchanged.

### Duplicate check

Exact VirtioFS issue and PR searches returned no results. #47412 proposes CephFS support through the same mechanism, but only for the separate `ceph` filesystem type. This PR does not include CephFS and can rebase around #47412 if it lands first.

items.title: fix(mooncake): Restore TP replication awareness for DCP and reduce write amplification
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation

When `dcp_size > 1`, `_spec_tp_replication_factor` unconditionally returns 1, forcing every TP rank to save every chunk — `tp_size`× write amplification (e.g. 8× under TP8+DCP4). This is correct but wastes store bandwidth and capacity.

### Changes

**Restore TP replication awareness** (`worker.py`):
- Remove the `if self.dcp_size > 1: return 1` override in `_spec_tp_replication_factor`, so the true factor is used (MLA=`tp_size`, GQA=`tp_size//num_kv_head`, Mamba=1).
- Generalize `put_step` to `max(1, group_put_steps[g_idx] // dcp_size)` so each chunk is saved by exactly one rank per DCP namespace, reducing write amplification from `tp_size`× to `dcp_size`×.
- Adjust `put_step_rank` to `(tp_rank // dcp_size + g_idx) % put_step` to stripe within each DCP subgroup.

**Explicit per-rank DCP namespace** (`worker.py`, `data.py`):
- Add `dcp_size`/`dcp_rank` to `KVCacheStoreSendingThread` and `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread`.
- `key_for()` gains an optional `dcp_rank` parameter; save and load pass `dcp_rank=self.dcp_rank` so each rank writes to its own namespace.
- Restructure `_init_lookup_key_prefixes` into `(shard_rank, dcp_rank, prefix)` tuples with separate TP-shard and DCP-namespace dimensions. Add `_lookup_num_shards` for the total shard count per group.

**Safety guards** (`worker.py`):
- Clamp `token_len` to `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size` before save (prevents `AssertionError` after external cache hit).
- Skip `NULL_BLOCK_ID` chunks during load (protects against abort races).
- Early return when all load chunks are filtered out (prevents `ZeroDivisionError`).

### Performance impact (MLA, TP8, DCP4)

| Metric | main | this PR |
|--------|------|----------|
| Write amplification | 8× per chunk | 2× per chunk |
| Lookup keys per chunk | 8 | 4 |
| Correctness | ✓ | ✓ |

### Production verification

Deployed to GLM-5.2 (TP8, DCP4, MLA): external prefix cache hit rate 28.3%, no regressions.

After [vllm#49714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49714), every decode step runs `nan_to_num_(-inf)` over the full

items.title: [BugFix] Mamba sparse retention keeps a state below each boundary under EAGLE/MTP
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #53504

Prefix caching never hits on hybrid models running MTP/EAGLE spec decode. Measured on GLM-5.3-Flash in production: 0 hit tokens against 16,897 queried, silently.

The full-attention EAGLE lookup drops one block below what it matched, but latest-only Mamba retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, the default) keeps only the state at the boundary itself, one block above anything a lookup can ever request. The reconciled hit is always 0.

Fix: when the group runs under EAGLE, also retain the state one block below each reachable boundary. Costs at most one extra state page per request; non-speculative behavior unchanged.

Verified live on a 4x DGX Spark GLM-5.3-Flash deployment (MTP k=3, TP=4): an identical 8,901-token resend now hits 4,608 tokens, warm TTFT 2.66 s vs 5.88 s cold, warm output byte-identical at temperature 0. # [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups

## Purpose

`build_offloading_config` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`) builds an `OffloadingGroupConfig` for **every** `kv_cache_group` and then asserts, for all of them:

```
assert group.tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0, (
    f"tokens_per_block={group.tokens_per_block} not divisible by "
    f"tokens_per_hash={tokens_per_hash}. "
    f"Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need "
    f"--enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes."
)
```

But `tokens_per_hash` comes from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which derives the hash granularity from **prefix-cacheable groups only** (`hashing_sizes = [... if group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable]`). The two sides disagree about which groups are in scope, so any hybrid model with a non-prefix-cacheable scratch group (`CircularBufferSpec.prefix_cacheable == False`) whose block size does not divide the cacheable groups' hash granularity crashes at boot the moment the OffloadingConnector is enabled:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=16. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Enabling prefix caching does not help — the message's advice cannot be followed, because the scratch group is excluded from hash-size resolution *by design* and its ring capacity is set by compression/lookahead geometry, not by the cache block size.

Where this bites: sparse-MLA hybrids that keep a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of pre-compression keys. Fixes #54907 and follows the GLM-5.3 report in #50095.

NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 dense prefill consumes normalized/rotated K outputs on every DCP rank. ## Purpose

DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2) currently have **no working sparse-attention backend on
consumer Blackwell** (SM12x: RTX 5090, GB10): the native FlashMLA sparse kernels
(`vllm._flashmla_C`) only build for sm90/sm100, and the sole SM12x option,
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, livelocks under sustained load — GPUs pin at 100 % with zero
output until the NCCL watchdog kills the server. Fixes #51921 (on SM12x).

This makes the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend work on SM12x by binding portable **Triton**
implementations of `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` when the native extension
can't serve the device. The kernels are from #49026 (@marksunner, validated there on
sm_121/GB10) — this PR is that work rebased onto current main as a first-class code path
instead of that PR's runtime monkeypatch, with its model-side diffs dropped (main already has
that content). Supersedes/continues #49026 — happy to hand back or co-drive.

Changes:
- `ops/flashmla.py`: `_use_triton_sparse_mla()` (auto on SM12x; `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`
  forces on/off) selects the Triton binding; `is_flashmla_sparse_supported()` reports True

  `ops/deepseek_v4_ops/*` — kernels + helpers from #49026, unchanged.
- `flashmla_sparse.py`: capability 12 allowed on the Triton path; %16 fp8-decode head padding

items.title: [Security] Cap GLMGA video sampling to prevent request-driven resource exhaustion
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- Add hard class-level upper bounds (`_MAX_FRAMES=640`, `_MAX_FPS=30`) to `GLMGAVideoBackend` so that request-controlled `fps` and `max_frames` values via `media_io_kwargs` cannot create disproportionately large intermediate list allocations.
- Clamp `extract_t` to `total_frames_num`, ensuring the index list never exceeds the actual frame count of the video, regardless of sampling parameters.
- Add regression tests verifying extreme values are bounded and normal operation is unchanged.

## Root Cause

`GLMGAVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` computes `extract_t = min(int(duration * target_fps), max_frames)` where both `target_fps` and `max_frames` are controllable via request-level `media_io_kwargs`. When `total_frames_num < extract_t`, a list comprehension with `range(extract_t)` creates an attacker-sized intermediate allocation (e.g. 500k entries for a 2-frame video) that is subsequently deduplicated to just the actual frame count.

## Fix

Three layers of defense, following the pattern established by `GLM46VVideoBackend`:

1. **Cap `target_fps`** to `_MAX_FPS` (30) -- request values above this are clamped.
2. **Cap `max_frames`** to `_MAX_FRAMES` (640) -- request values above this are clamped.
3. **Clamp `extract_t` to `total_frames_num`** -- the critical invariant: there can never be more unique frame indices than there are frames in the video.

## Test Plan

- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_extreme_values_bounded_by_total_frames` -- 2-frame video with fps=500k, max_frames=500k produces at most 2 indices.
- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_class_cap_overrides_kwargs_max_frames` -- max_frames=100k from kwargs is clamped to 640.
- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_class_cap_overrides_target_fps` -- fps=500k is clamped to 30.
- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_normal_operation_unchanged` -- normal 1000-frame video with fps=2 produces expected results.

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] GLM-4.7: stray arg tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a tool-call corruption in the GLM-4.7 parser: stray `arg_key` markup leaks into the parsed argument **key**, so the client rejects the call.

Observed in production against a GLM server run with `--tool-call-parser glm47`:

```
list_dir({"path</arg_key>": "/Users/user/Desktop/project"})
-> client error: "must have required property 'path'"
```

The client rejects the call, the agent loses the step, and the model retries with an invented path.

**Root cause.** `_glm47_arg_converter` matched the key with an unbounded non-greedy group:

```python
r"<arg_key>(?P<key>.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(?P<value>.*?)</arg_value>"
```

`.*?` is non-greedy but it is *not* bounded by the delimiter it is scanning for. If the stream contains a repeated or stray `arg_key` tag, the engine backtracks past the first `</arg_key>` because that is what it takes to reach the following `<arg_value>`, and the extra markup ends up inside the key. On

```
<arg_key>path</arg_key></arg_key><arg_value>/tmp/x</arg_value>
```

the old code yields `{"path</arg_key>": "/tmp/x"}`, reproducing the observed string exactly. The mirrored `<arg_key><arg_key>path…` case yields `{"<arg_key>path": "/tmp/x"}`.

**Fix.** Match runs of non-`<` text so the key group cannot cross its own delimiter, and accept a run of closing tags so a duplicate is skipped rather than shifting the key:

```python
_ARG_KEY = r"<arg_key>(?P<key>[^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
```

Both `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` are built from it, so the streaming path gets the same guarantee.

The unrolled possessive form is deliberate rather than the simpler tempered dot `(?:(?!</?arg_key>).)*`. `_compute_arg_delta` re-runs the converter over the whole accumulated buffer on every argument chunk, so the common streaming case is a *failing* match against a partial buffer — precisely where a tempered dot backtracks per character. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`_nvfp4_compute_scale_factor` in `marlin_utils_fp4.py` finds the largest NVFP4 weight scale by materializing an FP32 copy of the whole scale tensor, a boolean mask, and a gathered copy of the positive entries. The MoE paths (`prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin`, `prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin`) call it on the scales of **all experts at once**, so for a 288-expert model such as GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 one call touches about 300M elements and allocates several GiB of transient device memory during weight loading. On unified-memory machines with little headroom at load time (DGX Spark GB10, #50925) that spike can fail the load or push the driver into the memory-pressure spiral reported by the community.

This PR reduces the input tensor directly. The returned factor is unchanged:

- a max commutes with the exact multiplication by `2**7`;
- non-positive scales never win the max when a positive scale exists, and an all-non-positive tensor still returns `1.0`;
- an empty tensor returns `1.0` as before.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

- add a version-aware merged-weight cache key in the KDA layer

- add explicit invalidation hooks for the merged KDA cache

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3 kpool top-k can produce fewer valid entries than the allocated `select_k` width for short rows. The kernels do not promise to write the remaining slots, so allocating `pool_topk` with `torch.empty` can leave arbitrary positive values that are later treated as pool IDs and expanded into out-of-range sparse-attention token indices.

This change adds two defensive layers:

1. Initialize the prefill and decode pool-topk destinations with the `-1` sentinel.
2. Reject pool IDs outside the completed-pool count in the NVIDIA and AMD fused expansion kernels and in the current prefill fallback.

The regression covers valid pool IDs, negative sentinels, positive out-of-range IDs, and an incomplete tail. Only tokens from valid completed pools and the legitimate tail survive.

This was originally developed in https://github.com/ZJY0516/vllm/pull/8 while https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53906 was still pending. Now that #53906 is merged, this is the upstream-main version.

Before opening this PR, I searched open PRs for references to #53906, `GLM kpool invalid indices`, `pool_topk expand_pools`, and the broader `kpool` term. No open PR carries this exact sentinel initialization plus completed-pool bounds check.

## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but

  different failure.

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM] Invalidate merged KDA convolution weights after refit
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

## Fix

- add a version-aware merged-weight cache key in the KDA layer
- rebuild the merged tensor when any source conv weight changes
- add explicit invalidation hooks for the merged KDA cache
- invoke cache invalidation before GLM-5.3 weight loading so the next access rebuilds from fresh weights

## Purpose

Fix ROCm sparse-MLA dispatch for GLM-5.3-Flash during multi-token speculative decoding.

The existing selector routes ordinary BF16 rope-free decode through the Triton ragged kernel, but excludes speculative verification rows when `max_query_len > 1` or `num_decode_tokens != num_decodes`. Those rows consequently fall through to an incompatible AITER kernel and **produce corrupted output leading to 0% correct on GSM8k.**

This implements the geometry-based dispatch proposed in [vLLM issue #53943](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53943#issuecomment-5450595617).

## Changes

- Select the Triton ragged sparse-MLA path for all active BF16 rope-free prefill and decode rows.
- Add regression coverage for multi-token speculative verification shapes.
- Preserve the existing FP8 dispatch behavior.

## Test results

Focused unit tests:

- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py`
- 15 passed

GSM8K on 4× MI355X, TP=4:

- Eager baseline: 91.13%
- Full graphs, no MTP: 90.67%
- Full graphs with MTP5: 91.74%
- Weighted draft acceptance: 62.7%
- MTP5 runtime: 153.1s versus 173.0s without MTP

Before this fix, the MTP5 run produced corrupted repeated-token output and effectively 0% accuracy.

## Related issues

- Addresses the MTP dispatch failure documented in [#53943](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53943#issuecomment-5450595617).

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Warm up the Triton fused MoE GEMMs
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_moe_kernel` is the expert GEMM whenever DeepGEMM declines the shape. The
dominant case is the `N <= 512` early-out in `_valid_deep_gemm`
(`experts/deep_gemm_moe.py`): a model with a small `moe_intermediate_size`
crosses that threshold as soon as TP is high enough, and from then on never uses
DeepGEMM. GLM-5.2-FP8 at TP=8 gives `w2 = (256, 6144, 256)`, i.e. `N=256`, so its
whole MoE stack runs on Triton for every request.

Nothing in the startup path compiles that kernel for the variants real batches
select. Two things vary with the token count `M`:

1. the tile config, chosen by `try_get_optimal_moe_config` from a tuned config
   file or `get_default_config`;
2. the 16-divisibility of `EM` and `num_valid_tokens`, which Triton attaches as
   a `tt.divisibility` attribute and keys separately.

Profiling and CUDA graph capture only reach a few of these combinations, so the
first request landing on an uncompiled one JIT-compiles mid-serving. Measured on
GLM-5.2-FP8 at TP=8, main compiles 4 distinct variants per rank during
inference (32 events across 8 ranks). With `--jit-monitor-mode=error` that is a
hard failure; with the default `warn` it is a latency spike.

## Changes

- New `vllm/model_executor/warmup/triton_moe_warmup.py`: walks the `M` values
  that can select a distinct tile config, pairs each with a neighbour of
  opposite parity so both divisibility variants compile, and runs the expert
  GEMMs through `TritonExperts.apply` once per value.
- Called from `kernel_warmup` inside the existing `enable_jit_warmup` block.

Design notes:

- Warmup drives `TritonExperts.apply` rather than reconstructing the ~30 kernel
  arguments. `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` derives the strides, `EM`,
  `SWAP_AB` and the effective `BLOCK_SIZE_K` from the tensors it is handed, so
  going through the real path is the only way to guarantee the compiled key
  matches the serving key. A compile-only draft built on `TritonWarmupTensor`
  was discarded for that reason

items.title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: pass varlen indices to the kpool paged MQA logits (fixes MTP decode hang)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix the GPU-side decode hang of GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP speculative decoding on SM100 (all GPUs at 100% utilization, worker threads idle, engine dies on `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` ~30 min later).

A user-triggered CUDA core dump of the hung workers (`CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP`, then `cuda-gdb target cudacore`) shows a single live CTA of `deep_gemm::sm100_fp8_paged_mqa_logits<kNextN=1, ..., kIsVarlen=false>` whose math warps spin on the Q-stage mbarrier after the TMA producer warp has exited.

Cause: on SM100 `DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder` schedules the paged MQA logits in varlen mode (per-token rows tagged with request indices, `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(..., indices=...)`), and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` passes `indices=decode_metadata.indices` to the kernel. The kpool indexer did not, so DeepGEMM ran the non-varlen `next_n=1` kernel on a varlen schedule. Under MTP the varlen scheduler pairs adjacent rows of a request into one atom charged with the later row's context length, while the non-varlen walk treats every row as its own request and stops only on an exact `(q_atom, kv_split)` end match. As soon as a pair straddles a 256-state split boundary (1024 tokens at `index_kpool=4`) the walk steps past an end marker it can never hit, the TMA warp stops prefetching Q and the math warps wait forever on the Q-stage barrier. Single-token decode has one row per request, so both schedules coincide and non-MTP serving never hit it; short prompts never straddle a split, which is why synthetic loads did not reproduce it and GSM8K 5-shot did within minutes.

Duplicate check: #55201 touches the kpool top-k sentinel handling, not this call; no open PR passes `indices` here.

GLM-5.3-Flash on GB200, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, GSM8K 5-shot x2 (2638 requests, concurrency 32):

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Make the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` backend usable for GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, #53906), whose sparse MLA layers are NoPE (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`) with a kpool-widened top-k buffer. Two independent breakages are fixed:

1. **`concat_and_cache` fp8_ds_mla rejects NoPE rows.** The packed fp8_ds_mla row layout is unchanged for NoPE models (512B latent + 16B tile scales + 128B reserved RoPE/padding = 656B), but the host check required `pe_dim == 64` and the kernel's RoPE warp assumed 64 tail elements. Relax the check to `pe_dim ∈ {64, 0}` and make the RoPE warp exit early when `pe_dim == 0`; the reserved bytes stay untouched padding, which the FlashInfer GLM53_NOPE kernels never read.

2. **Sparse page-table sized by `topk_tokens` instead of the actual buffer width.** GLM-5.3-Flash widens the top-k buffer past `index_topk` with a kpool tail (2048 → 2176, rounded to a multiple of 128), so `topk_indices_physical.shape[1] != attn_metadata.topk_tokens` and FlashInfer rejects `block_tables (B, 1, 2176)` against `sparse_mla_top_k=2048`. Mirror the generic `flashinfer_mla_sparse` backend: derive `sparse_mla_top_k`/`max_seq_len` from the converted buffer width; the kernel treats it as page-table capacity and bounds the active length by the `-1` padding.

No behavior change for DSv3.2/DSv4 (RoPE, kpool=1): the packed row write is identical when `pe_dim == 64`, and `shape[1] == topk_tokens` when there is no kpool tail.

Requires FlashInfer with GLM53_NOPE support plus the companion check-scoping fix flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4947 — both ride the same post-flashinfer#4802 release boundary, so no additional wait.
